key_facts: The layer between the skin and abdominal wall muscles is the subcutaneous tissue (superficial fascia).
On CT, normal subcutaneous fat is hypoattenuating relative to muscle and solid organs.
Subcutaneous tissue can contain fat lobules, small vessels, and connective tissue septa.
In the abdomen, deeper structures include the abdominal wall muscles, peritoneal cavity, bowel loops, psoas muscles, and retroperitoneal vessels.
Diffuse increased attenuation in this layer can indicate edema or inflammation.
